capabilities.line: Start a job with a chat: it proposes a plan, and nothing starts until you confirm it. Or pick a built-in kind of job.
Understand: pick the repos and ask how your code fits together; a read-only analysis answers and cites the files it read.
While a step works you see who is responding, and the live tool calls, edits and reported cost.
A job’s questions and decisions come to you as one guided card, with a 10-second undo on gate decisions.
Built-in editors: write a document in place and export a PDF, edit and reorder slides, trim captioned demo recordings.
Learn turns your team docs, your best repos and your writing into suggested rules and memories; you choose which become active.

Evaluate replays good and bad examples of agent behaviour against your enforcing rules: what they catch, what slips through, and which rules the examples never exercised (recall-only guidance is not measured).
The main pages, including Understand, Report, Evaluate, Steering, Memory, Learn and Nerve Center, each have a chat over their own data.
Voice: with whisper.cpp installed, speech becomes text on your machine, and the audio is never stored. Nothing is sent to a job until you confirm it on screen.
Wicked Dark, Wicked Light and Ambient: a quiet line and tint that follow the state of your work.
New job opens on a catalog of job types you can search and filter by category, with the ones you start most near the top; the chat’s slash menu lists the same entries.
Apps, under Work: describe a live app or dashboard over your databases in a chat. Each message is one change that a different agent reviews; then edit it in place, with undo and redo.

Data sources: connect Postgres or MySQL, upload a SQLite file, or add a GraphQL API; Test connection says how long it took and whether TLS is verified. An app writes database rows only to Postgres, with Allow writes on.
Ask a question of the data: an agent drafts one read-only query and says what it does, and nothing runs until you confirm it.
The Agents box on a saved SQL source: whether agents may see its structure and, on Postgres, query its rows; in which projects (none until you pick one); and their recent queries.
Understand’s Knowledge map draws your data sources, repositories and linked trackers, with the data shapes you approved; a shape is drawn only after you approve it.
Linked trackers on a project or a repository: GitHub Issues and Jira, one or several, and a job can start from an issue.
Report shows up to four apps you switch on as dashboards, with live numbers; Build a dashboard starts a new app by chat.
Sign each agent in once on the Agents page: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode or Pi.
Agents work in sandboxes by default: every capability dropped, a read-only root, and one way out, the model gateway.
Your keys stay in a broker and the sandbox sees placeholders. A Claude subscription’s sign-in token is the one exception, and a guard keeps it out of the delivered work.
Needs a container runtime: Docker, Podman, Rancher Desktop, Colima or OrbStack.
When you launch a preset or a plan on a repository, the code-writing step runs as one agent’s checkpointed turns, with rigor re-scored from the diff (power mode, on by default).
“Check on it?”: a different agent reads a long step’s record and recommends; if none can, crew gives its own labelled reading. It changes nothing.
By default a different agent reviews the work. When none can, the job stops unless you launch it as reduced assurance, which is labelled on the job, every gate and the delivery.
In power mode a failed review or a qualifying build-check failure goes back to the builder, up to three hand-off attempts in all. A phased job retries, escalates or stops.
Feature, bug-fix, migration, MCP-server and editor-plugin jobs pass acceptance testing before delivery, unless a labelled waiver or skip says otherwise.
Gates say plainly what a pass means: “approved by default, not verified”, “reduced assurance”, “QE acceptance skipped by operator”.
The evidence: who built it, who checked it, what ran and what was skipped. With PR delivery on a supported remote, you get a PR.
A job can propose what it learned, with its source job; you approve what becomes memory.
Built-in jobs design, build, test and install an MCP server or a studio editor plugin; the install waits for your consent.
Sandbox images: on Docker, protected from the runtime’s automatic cleanup; a missing built-in image is rebuilt on next use.
Agents read a live data source only through one gate: read-only SQL checked before it runs, a 10-second deadline, at most 200 rows and 64 KB, and every result marked untrusted and cited.
Every gate and delivery records which data sources the job’s agents read, or says it is not known.
Agents never get a source’s connection details or stored secret: they get agent-safe views of the registry, the apps and the audit trail.
A job reaches only its project’s and its repositories’ trackers, and its delivery links back to the issue in the tracker’s own form.
Apps are kept as versions with receipts. An app’s actions call an API or write a database row only when a person confirms; row writes go to Postgres only, with Allow writes on.
Jobs defined as data: it plans the steps, decides which agent builds and, by default, which different agent reviews, and records every verdict.
Runs your repository’s own detected or configured checks; where supported it compares them with the base, so a new failure denies verification.
Builds a repository’s requirements graph and measures real coverage against a minimum; placeholders never count.
A single-writer store owns the SQLite file, so the daemon, the UI and the MCP servers share one command API and a live event stream.
Ships the skills every agent in a wicked-crew job follows.
A proof gate re-checks “done” from evidence: an unsupported claim is rejected, and by default it fails closed when its checks cannot run.
40 QE specialists, including an acceptance pipeline that keeps the writer, the executor and the reviewer apart.
With wicked-estate’s code graph it sees the event and command links grep never sees, and renames across files as a graph operation.
A disputed decision goes to a review panel of your other agents; a same-family fallback is labelled, and without a quorum there is no verdict.
In a wicked-crew job, every agent is asked to propose what it witnessed, as a memory for you to approve.
Works in Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode and Pi, in CI, or inside a wicked-crew job.
Domain mapping keeps going page after page until real requirements reach the target, and asks before it spends more.
The apps skill builds an app as data from your sources’ structure and never calls a write tool; a live read goes through crew’s data gate.
The data skill proposes data shapes (what a table joins, which code describes it) for you to approve; it never reads a row.
A code graph over 114 languages (depth varies by language), with blast radius and the event and command links grep never sees.
A local CLI and MCP server: a catalog of 33 standard MCP tools (read-only mode and unavailable stores reduce the set offered), plus semantic search when enabled.
Memory you can read, kept apart from knowledge. Memories about how you work can apply across projects; project memories stay with their project.
Local SQLite with no database server to run; a shared PostgreSQL code graph is an optional CLI build for a team.
Did you mean…? A missed symbol name gets suggestions. Prebuilt binaries for five platforms on every GitHub release.
Knowledge holds your data sources’ structure, never their rows, and the data shapes you approve, linked to the code that describes them.
Recall returns only what the asker may see: each item names the sources and repositories it came from.
Document storage with version history (version lineage).
Renders documents as HTML and exports them as PDF.
Captioned demo recordings of a live app: on-screen captions, no voice-over.
At-least-once delivery with restart-durable retry, dead-lettering with operator replay, and causality tracing.
Its durable store is embedded SQLite, so there is no server to run; single-host today.
An interactive installer for the whole family that knows which products depend on which.
Installs for Claude Code, Antigravity, Codex, OpenCode and Pi.
GitLab and Azure DevOps trackers.
More databases: SQL Server, Oracle, Snowflake and BigQuery.
Report’s own figures as a data source for your apps.
